subject: art-history
intro: Art history leads into the institutions that keep and interpret the world's visual heritage: curating collections, preserving archives and objects, researching the past and teaching it at university level.

roles.title: Curators
roles.what: Administer collections of artwork, collectibles, historic items or scientific specimens for museums or other institutions, and conduct the instructional, research and public service activities that surround them.
roles.where: The global survey from prehistory to global contemporary — cultural contexts, purpose and audience, theories and interpretations — is the scholarly grounding a curator needs to build and defend an exhibition.

roles.title: Archivists
roles.what: Appraise, edit and direct the safekeeping of permanent records and historically valuable documents, and participate in research activities based on archival materials.
roles.where: The course's source-analysis habits — materials and techniques, interactions across cultures, dating and attribution — train the critical handling of primary material archives exist to preserve.

roles.title: Museum Technicians and Conservators
roles.entry: Master's degree typical; technician roles vary
roles.what: Restore, maintain or prepare objects in museum collections for storage, research or exhibit, working with artifacts, textiles or art, and identifying, recording and installing objects in exhibits.
roles.where: The materials, processes and techniques strands threaded through every content area — from prehistoric media to contemporary installation — teach exactly the object literacy conservation demands.

roles.title: Historians
roles.what: Research, analyse, record and interpret the past as recorded in government and institutional records, newspapers, photographs, interviews, films and unpublished manuscripts such as personal diaries and letters.
roles.where: The theories-and-interpretations units train reading artefacts as evidence; the course's attention to purpose and audience across ten world regions is historical method applied to visual culture.

roles.title: Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in drama, music and the arts, including fine and applied art such as painting and sculpture or design and crafts — combining teaching with research into the discipline.
roles.where: The survey's ten content areas and its theories-and-interpretations spiral are the lecture-and-seminar stock of a university art history teaching post.
